summary: Iteration 28 tested (A) the client-admin contact editor (/api/client-contact, the Settings card and the contact block on the branded login screen) and (B) the cost-per-head chart for batches (rzuty). Backend: 13 of 13 pytest cases pass. They cover RBAC, superadmin client_id scoping, validation (email, phone, website, address length), the foreign-Origin guard, PATCH /api/clients contact, public branding contact and cost_per_head math with synthetic meter data. Frontend at 390px: everything passes. Client admin saves, the values survive a reload and they show up on /?klient=kowalski. The superadmin card follows the selected client's device. The chart renders, highlights the cheapest finished batch and fades the running one. The chart is hidden when a chamber has no cost data. All test data has been cleaned up. Kowalski contact and rates are restored and site data was not touched.

ui_bugs.issue: At 390px the Y-axis tick labels are cut off on the left (shown as '.18', '135', '.09', '045' instead of 0.18 / 0.135 ...). Caused by margin left:-18 together with YAxis width 44. The axis also uses '.' as the decimal separator while the bar labels use ','.

integration_issues.issue: The same contact data has two editors on one screen: FleetCard brand-contact-* and client-contact-card. Their state is not synced, so saving in one leaves the other stale, and saving the stale one later overwrites the newer values.

issues: The inputs have only placeholders and no labels. Once filled, it is not clear which field is which (website vs. address).
X-axis labels on the cost chart use yy-mm-dd ('26-09-15'), which is ambiguous for Polish users. Consider dd.mm or dd.mm.yy.

action_items: Fix the cut-off Y-axis ticks in CycleCostChart on mobile (raise the left margin to about 0 or widen the YAxis, and use a tickFormatter with a Polish comma).
Optional: sync or reload FleetCard contact after a ClientContactCard save (or the other way round), or drop the duplicate editor for the selected client.
Optional: add labels or icons to the contact inputs and use a dd.mm date format on the chart's X axis.
critical_code_review_comments: Mutations are protected by an Origin guard. No X-CSRF-Token check exists in server.py, so the credential notes mentioning the CSRF header are misleading (harmless).
For a client admin, PUT /api/client-contact?client_id=<other> silently ignores client_id and writes to the admin's own client. This is safe, but the client could return 403 for clarity.
PUT /client-contact overwrites all four fields. The frontend always sends all of them, so this is fine.
